title: Allocation Sprint Lanes and Contingency Tranches Framework
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Create a repeatable framework to allocate sprint lanes (core, tactical, buffer) and define contingency tranches for mid-cycle shock handling. This will help product and engineering make defensible scope cuts, reserve surge staffing, and communicate trade-offs to stakeholders.

Background: We consistently see mid-cycle interrupts (incidents, partner requests, urgent compliance work) that force reactive de-scoping. Current practices rely on ad-hoc buffers and PM judgement which leads to uneven customer impact and frequent scope churn.

Objectives:
- Define 3 lane types with clear entry/exit rules: Core (must-deliver), Tactical (value-driven stretch), Buffer (reserved for emergent work).
- Standardize contingency tranches (% of team capacity, roles involved, activation triggers).
- Produce a lightweight decision matrix for scope cuts tied to OKR marginal value, customer impact, and engineering cost.
- Provide handoffs and communication templates for CTO/PM/Eng leads when tranches are activated.

Outcomes / Acceptance criteria:
- A one-page framework doc and a 1-hour training for PM/Eng leads approved by Head of Product and Eng.
- Pilot applied to two teams in Cycle 2026-W11 with explicit metrics tracked (scope slippage, mean time to activate tranche, stakeholder satisfaction).
- Two template responses for customers and internal stakeholders when a tranche is activated.

Approach / Implementation plan:
1) Week 0 (Discovery): Collect 6 months of cycle-level incidents and mid-cycle reprioritizations; interview 8 PM/Eng leads.
2) Week 1 (Draft): Create lane definitions, contingency % bands (suggested 8-12% baseline), and decision matrix.
3) Week 2 (Review): Cross-functional review with Legal, Sales for customer-facing constraints, and Design for messaging templates.
4) Week 3 (Pilot): Run with two teams; collect telemetry.
5) Week 6 (Iterate): Update framework and roll to broader org.

Risks / Trade-offs:
- Reserving too much capacity increases time-to-market; reserving too little reduces resilience. We'll propose a conservative 8% baseline and allow teams to opt-in up to 12% based on risk profile.
- Cultural change: PMs may default to protect scope; we will require explicit gating criteria and quarterly retro to adjust.

Stakeholders: Head of Product (Anika Rao), Head of Engineering (Liam O'Connor), Customer Success (Diego Alvarez), Legal (Priya Nair).

Artifacts and links:
- Draft framework doc: https://drive.google.com/open?id=framework-draft-2026
- Interview notes folder: https://drive.google.com/open?id=interviews-2026
